the characterization of a panel of MAbs recognizing three distinct melanoma cell surface associated antigens.

the equilibrium association constant (Ka) values obtained for these MAbs were in the range of 10(7)-10(10)M-1 and the maximum MAb binding value (Qmax) values were in the range 2 x 104-2 x 106 MAb molecules bound/cell.
these MAbs bind to their respective antigens with high affinity and in a manner consistent with a single binding site per molecule of antigen.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the MAb 43-2 recognizes a single binding site on the melanoma cell surface with a single K value, while the other MAbs recognize multiple sites, with the exception of the MAb 9.2.53 which appears to recognize a single site.

the equilibrium binding characteristics of MAbs recognizing melanoma cell associated antigens are similar to the equilibrium binding characteristics observed with MAbs recognizing tumor associated antigens in general.
the MAb 125kD/43.3, which recognizes the 125kdal MAA, is a high affinity antibody, whereas the MAb 43-2, which recognizes the HMW- MAA, is a low affinity antibody.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the binding characteristics of MAbs recognizing melanoma cell antigens are highly dependent on the cell lines used and the experimental conditions employed.
the binding of MAbs to melanoma cells is a highly complex process that is affected by a variety of factors.
the use of a single cell line to determine equilibrium binding parameters may be misleading.
